facts: The work proposes a new research direction.
The new research direction addresses the lack of structures in traditional n-gram models.
The work is based on a weakly supervised dependency parser.
The weakly supervised dependency parser can model speech syntax.
The weakly supervised dependency parser does not rely on any annotated training corpus.
Labeled data is replaced by a few hand-crafted rules.
The hand-crafted rules encode basic syntactic knowledge.
Bayesian inference combines the rules to create complex tree structures.
The complex tree structures maximize a discriminative model's posterior.
The posterior is on a target unlabeled corpus.
The posterior encodes sparse selectional preferences between a head word and its dependents.
The model is evaluated on English newspaper texts.
The model is evaluated on Czech newspaper texts.
The model is validated on French broadcast news transcriptions.
entities: lack of structures in traditional n-gram models
